text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The launch of a new communist party is in the interest of the ruling Socialist Party, keen rid itself of accusations that it represents the former Communist Party of late Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha.
- Albanian Defence Minister Sabit Broka said police had succeeded in locating some 16 rockets that unknown people had stolen last month in the southern town of Gjirokaster.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano asked President Rexhep Meidani to award the Mother Teresa medal to the commander of the multinational force Alba, Luciano Forlani.
- Fatos Lubonja, a former political prisoner and prominent writer turned down an offer to become general director of the state-run television.
- Some 60 policemen in the southern town of Fier failed to catch a criminal gang coming from the town of Vlore.

- Right-wing parties insist that the death penalty should be retained while the leftists want to adapt Albanian legislation in line with the Council of Europe's guidelines which dropped the death penalty.
- The Organisation for Security and cooperation in Europe (OSCE) says it will continue to assist Albania, mostly in improving its legal system.
- The paper alleges that warships were ordered to move to the port town of Vlore from Durres in March in order to crack down on armed anti-government demonstrators.
- The Democratic Party has opened an office to assist public servants fired by socialist-led ruling coalition.
- The Red Cross said it had provided some 25,000 Albanian families with relief aid over the past five months.
- Albanian Defence Minister Sabit Broka said that the Intelligence Service (Shik) should be held responsible for the destruction of the national army.
